_comment:
Something big falls over. A PROP role with no needsAnyOf, so it plays on a tower, a wardrobe, a statue, a stack of crates — anything on stage.

The hard constraint: a whole actor CANNOT be rotated, only moved. So the fall is faked the way limited animation has always faked it — the prop slides sideways and DOWN in one eased move and the sound does the rest. boom on the impact frame, crumble a third of a second later as the debris settles, a hard camera shake, and smoke plus a dust burst at the base.

All of the comedy is in the 0.5 seconds where nothing happens. It creaks a hair the wrong way (dx -0.008), teeters back the OTHER way past its balance point (dx +0.016, then +0.020), and then HANGS there. A fall with no hang is a glitch; a fall with a hang is a joke. Nothing lands inside 0.17s of the beat before it — 12fps forgives nothing.

Triggers stay clear of "keels over"/"keeled over": those are idiomatically a PERSON going down, they belong to the cast gag `faint`, and because this gag asks for nothing and sits above faint in the index it would win them every time and drop a crate instead of the character. It DOES deliberately share "topples over"/"comes crashing down" with `collapse`, which sits ABOVE it and needs a `collapse` clip: that is the specific-above-fallback ladder, and this is the tier-1-3 fallback that plays when the prop cannot collapse.

Ends by standing it back up on the cut. Position carries to the end of the scene, so a prop left lying at dx -0.24 is a prop in the wrong place for every shot afterwards; a wreck that PERSISTS is the job of a rig pose, which this tier does not use.

object._comment: No needsAnyOf. Whatever prop the scene has staged can fall over; nothing has to be declared for it.

beats._comment: the groan of something shifting on its base, before anything is visibly wrong
a hair the way it is ABOUT to go. dx/dy are offsets from the mark this role bound to, so the restore at the end is simply back to zero.
the anticipation: it leans the WRONG way first. Every fall in animation is preceded by a lean in the opposite direction.
creeps a further 0.004 past the balance point and then STOPS. 0.5s of dead air follows — this hold is the gag.
the fall itself: one eased whole-actor move, sideways and down together. There is no rotate channel for a whole actor, so the arc is entirely in this diagonal plus the audio.
impact, at the end of the 0.34s fall
the dust punch. Offset 0.06 from the smoke so they read as two events, not one mush.
debris settling AFTER the impact — the detail that gives the thing weight
the settle rock: a tiny bounce back up the way it came. Heavy things do not stop dead.
scene hygiene on the cut frame, not eased. Position carries to the end of the SCENE.
